relation: grant(principal, grantee, scope, window, nonce) -> { verdict: granted }
description: The delegation rule: what makes a mandate-morpheme a valid grant of verdict authority (W-11). A mandate's R resolves here; its bindingHash is the mandateHash every mandated verdict cites. Authority that cannot be revoked was never granted - it was surrendered.
constraints: The grantee never signs payer testimony (restates W-2). No mandate can grant what the architecture forbids: the payer signs their own stamp, always, on every lane.

The grantee never renders success verdicts - the stamp is the verdict. This clause is load-bearing: success needing no verdict is what keeps D-6's lazy-attestation economics closed. A delegation rule without it silently reopens the drain vector.

The mandate chain is depth-1: ORG root (self-grounding, no mandateHash in M) -> operator. Recursive delegation is reserved to Coprocessor I-9 and the D-7 roadmap. A mandate whose principal is not the root is out of scope for this build's verifier.

grantValidity.check: principal and grantee are distinct accounts - a self-granted mandate is not a grant

the principal is the registry's root: enforced by the network, not by content - only the root key can write to the Witness Rule Registry (immutable submit key, V-11), so a mandate's presence on the registry IS its principal's signature
grantValidity.onFailure: unwritable - the network refuses the message at consensus

grantValidity.check: scope is exactly { verdictClass, topicId } with verdictClass in the closed space ['rejection-attestation'] - nothing richer in MVP
grantValidity.onFailure: mandate.scope-mismatch (at verdict time, against the verdict's class and topic)

grantValidity.check: the window is non-empty: notBefore < notAfter when notAfter is present; both consensus-style timestamps. A verdict is in-window when its own consensus timestamp falls in [notBefore, revocation-or-notAfter) - half-open, judged with exact arithmetic, never against query-time state (W-12)
a nonce is present: mandate identity is content-derived (the bindingHash), so a revoked grant's identity is permanently dead and re-granting requires fresh content

revocation: a root-submitted mandateRevocation naming this mandateHash ends the window at the revocation's consensus timestamp - effective from that instant, never retroactive; verdicts rendered in-window stand forever
grantValidity.onFailure: mandate.out-of-window (for verdicts at or after the revocation instant)

verdictClause.success: verdict 'granted', sealed as the mandate's O - the only success verdict in the witness layer, and it grants only the authority to render failures
verdictClause.unresolvable: a verdict citing a mandateHash that does not resolve on the registry (verified by recomputation, never by claim) is out-of-mandate: mandate.unresolvable
